newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK banks welcome safety net of Mortgage Corp.
newsitem.headline: HK banks welcome safety net of Mortgage Corp.

text.p: Senior Hong Kong bankers on Wednesday welcomed plans for the formation of a mortgage corporation, which they said should provide a safety net for banks at a time when their property exposure is ballooning.
"I think it will be a good safety net for Hong Kong and I am all in favor of the Mortgage Corporation," said David Li, chairman of the Bank of East Asia at a seminar.
"It will also be a competitor of ours, but we need competitors," he said.
Ian Wilson, general manager for Hong Kong, China and Northeast Asia for Standard Chartered Bank agreed, and said the formation of the corporation was part of the development of a mature market.
"Banks that are finding that they're getting a concentration in their portfolio of too many mortgages as a percentage of their other loans (will have) an escape route," Wilson said.

Hong Kong's de-facto central bank, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), will set up and run the Mortgage Corp which is aimed at easing the mismatch of funding between long-term lending and short-term borrowing, and improving financing flows for home ownership.
The Mortgage Corporation will acquire mortgage loans from banks for its own portfolio and then issue mortgage-backed securities.

The HKMA expressed concern last month at the growth in mortgage lending in Hong Kong, which has increased banks' property exposure, and said additional restraints in mortgage lending policies may be required.
